name: 1Password
scope_notes: Covers 1Password Business. Covers 1Password.com Business/Enterprise developer and admin credentials; Connect server and SCIM bridge are customer-hosted; CLI user sign-in is a human login and excluded except as client for service accounts.

controls.name: Service Account permission (who can create service accounts)
controls.what: Only owners/admins can create service accounts unless they grant the permission to groups or people.
controls.setting: Developer > Permissions > Service Account > Manage groups / Manage People

controls.name: Service Account Access (per vault)
controls.what: Turning off service account access on a vault removes it from all existing service accounts and blocks new grants.
controls.setting: Vault > Manage > Service Account Access toggle

controls.name: Vault permissions at creation
controls.what: Vaults and read/write/share permissions are chosen at creation and cannot be changed later.
controls.setting: Service account wizard / op service-account create --vault; Connect New Token

controls.name: Revoke Token
controls.what: Revoking a service account token immediately removes its vault access.
controls.setting: Developer > Service accounts > [account] > Token > Revoke Token

controls.name: Rotate Token
controls.what: Issues a new token and expires the old one now, in 1 hour, or in 3 days.
controls.setting: Developer > Service accounts > [account] > Token > Rotate Token

controls.name: --expires-in
controls.what: Sets a lifetime for a service account at creation via CLI.

controls.name: Secrets Automation managers / environment permissions
controls.what: Limits which groups can manage Connect servers and tokens, globally or per environment.

controls.name: Connect token Expires After
controls.what: Token is revoked automatically after 30, 90 or 180 days.
controls.setting: Developer > Connect servers > [environment] > New Token > Expires After

controls.name: Revoke (Connect token)
controls.what: Revokes a Connect server access token.

controls.name: Regenerate Credentials
controls.what: Issues a new SCIM bearer token and scimsession file.
controls.setting: Integrations > Automated User Provisioning > Regenerate Credentials

controls.name: Firewall policy
controls.what: Allow/report/deny sign-in attempts by IP, CIDR, country or anonymous IP; documented to block the SCIM bridge.

controls.name: Events to Report
controls.what: Limits a token to sign-in attempts, item usages and/or audit events.

controls.name: Expires After (Events token)
controls.what: Optional 30/90/180-day expiry; default Never.

controls.name: Revoke (Events token)
controls.what: Revokes an Events API bearer token.

controls.name: OAuth application scopes
controls.what: Scopes users.view, users.suspend, users.reactivate chosen at creation and fixed.

controls.name: Revoke integration
controls.what: Revokes the OAuth app, its client credentials and every access token issued to it.

controls.name: Rotate the client secret
controls.what: New client secret; old secret stays valid 6 hours.

controls.name: POST /v1/oauth/revoke
controls.what: Revokes a single access token before expiry.

controls.name: Events Reporting setup restricted to owners and administrators
controls.what: Only owners or administrators can set up an Events Reporting integration and get its tokens.

controls.name: Permissions to manage integrations
controls.what: Only owners, administrators, or Security group members with permission to manage integrations can create a Users API OAuth application.

no_control.what: Cannot edit an existing service account's vaults or permissions to narrow access; must revoke and recreate.
Connect tokens cannot be changed or updated; rotation means create new and revoke old.
Revoking an access token only via revoke endpoint or integration revoke; deleting the client on your platform leaves issued tokens valid until expiry.

controls_unknown: Whether Business firewall rules apply to service account, Connect, Events API or Users API requests.
Whether Unlock with SSO / IdP policies affect service accounts (service_account_sso_denied is undocumented).
Whether audit log records Connect token, Events API token, SCIM credential regeneration or OAuth application create/revoke (only service account and satoken events are listed).
Whether Events API, Users API or SCIM calls themselves are logged anywhere customer-visible.
Whether a revoked Connect token or regenerated SCIM token stops working immediately.
Whether the itemusages Events API feed includes service account item access (usage reports do).

authentication.summary: A service account is a non-human 1Password user. Its token (prefix ops_) carries the account unlock key, SRP verifier and keyset and is passed as OP_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_TOKEN to the CLI or SDKs.

federation.details: Service accounts have no email or password and are not tied to an IdP login. Docs do not say whether Unlock with SSO policies apply; the Events API lists a sign-in type service_account_sso_denied without explaining it.

ip_restriction.boundary: Business firewall rules allow/deny sign-in attempts by IP, country or anonymous IP. Docs do not say whether they apply to service account sign-ins.

lifetime.summary: No expiry unless set; CLI --expires-in at creation

renewal.expiry_basis: Token valid until revoked, deleted, or optional expiry
renewal.summary: Rotate Token issues a new token and lets the old one expire now, in 1 hour, or in 3 days.

administration.summary: Only owners/admins create service accounts by default; they can delegate to groups or people. Vault access and permissions are fixed at creation. Personal/Private/Employee/default Shared vaults are excluded.
administration.conditions: Delegated creators manage only their own service accounts; they need Manage Vault on vaults they grant.

offboard.details: A service account is its own user account for programmatic access, not tied to a team member's account.

inventory.details: 1Password.com Developer > Service accounts; owners and administrators can manage all service accounts on the team.

reads.ui: 1Password.com > Reports > Usage Report card > Create usage report > choose the service account
reads.api: POST /api/v2/itemusages (Events API; filter results on user.uuid = service account UUID)

token_format.notes: Base64-encoded JSON with email @1passwordserviceaccounts, secretKey, srpX, signInAddress.

log_sources.name: Audit log
log_sources.notes: Business; 365 days in UI; CSV export; also via Events API auditevents

log_sources.name: Usage report (service account / vault)
log_sources.notes: Business; item access with action and last access

credential_id_fields.notes: aux_info holds token name for satoken events
Service account is a user; exact representation not documented

anomaly_cues: New satoken created or rotated outside change windows
Service account reading many vaults/items (op item list fans out per vault)
Vault create by a service account

containment.steps: Developer > Service accounts > account > Revoke Token, or delete the service account; or turn off Service Account Access on affected vaults.
containment.notes: Docs: revoke immediately removes access; deleted SA token can't authenticate.

unknown: Whether individual CLI/SDK API calls are logged beyond item usage

calls.log_notes: Item access appears in usage reports (Business)

unknown: Whether whoami/list calls generate audit records

authentication.summary: Apps send a bearer token to a self-hosted Connect server. The server itself authenticates to 1Password with the 1password-credentials.json file. Tokens are ES256-signed and valid only for their server.

federation.details: Bearer token issued by 1Password; no IdP involvement documented.

ip_restriction.boundary: Connect server runs in customer infrastructure; network exposure is the customer's choice. No vendor IP control for tokens documented.

lifetime.summary: Optional 30/90/180 days; otherwise no expiry stated

renewal.expiry_basis: Tokens can't be changed; rotate by creating a new token and revoking the old
renewal.summary: Create new, update references, revoke old.

administration.summary: Secrets Automation managers (groups) and per-environment permissions control who manages Connect servers. Token vault list fixed at creation; max 100 vaults.
administration.conditions: Available to all 1Password customers since Feb 27, 2025.

inventory.details: 1Password.com Developer > Connect servers > (Secrets Automation environment) lists that environment's access tokens.

reads.api: POST /api/v2/itemusages (Events API; filter results on action = "server-fetch")

token_format.notes: JWT signed ES256 by the account key; jti is the token UUID.

log_sources.name: Connect GET /v1/activity
log_sources.notes: Per-server API request log with actor.jti, ip, userAgent, action, result

log_sources.name: Item usage report / itemusages
log_sources.notes: Used by = Connect server name, not token; action Display / server-fetch; can lose data when offline

anomaly_cues: Bursts of READ across many vaults

containment.steps: Developer > Connect servers > environment > gear > Revoke; or remove vault access from the environment.

unknown: Audit log event names for Connect token create/revoke

credentials.name: SCIM bridge / automated provisioning bearer token

authentication.summary: The IdP calls the SCIM bridge (self-hosted) or 1Password-hosted provisioning with a bearer token. On a self-hosted bridge the token is paired with the scimsession file that holds the bridge's 1Password credentials.

federation.details: Static bearer token configured in the IdP.

ip_restriction.boundary: Account firewall rules can block the self-hosted bridge's connection to 1Password; IdP-to-bridge traffic is the customer's network. Hosted provisioning not covered.

renewal.summary: Regenerate Credentials on the Integrations page; redeploy scimsession and update IdP token.

administration.summary: Owners/admins set up provisioning under Integrations > Automated User Provisioning. Hosted provisioning won't manage groups with Recover Accounts or Manage All Groups.

offboard.details: The bearer token belongs to the SCIM bridge deployment, paired with its scimsession file, not to a user.

anomaly_cues: Unexpected user provisioning or group membership changes
Firewall block messages in bridge log

containment.steps: Integrations > Automated User Provisioning > Regenerate Credentials, or turn off Provisioning users & groups.
containment.notes: Old token invalidation not explicitly stated.

authentication.summary: JWT bearer token issued from an Events Reporting integration, scoped to auditevents, itemusages and/or signinattempts. Read-only access to account activity.

ip_restriction.boundary: No IP restriction for Events API tokens documented.

renewal.expiry_basis: Issue a replacement token, then revoke
renewal.summary: Add a token, update SIEM, revoke old.

administration.summary: Owners/admins create Events Reporting integrations and issue/revoke tokens under Integrations.

offboard.details: Tokens belong to an Events Reporting integration, not to a user.

inventory.details: 1Password.com Integrations > (Events Reporting integration) > Tokens section lists each token, its events and expiry.

token_format.notes: JWT (eyJ...); introspect returns uuid of the token.

anomaly_cues: Unexpected new token on an Events Reporting integration
Token with Never expiry and all features

containment.steps: Integrations > Events Reporting integration > gear > Revoke.
containment.notes: Docs say SIEM stops ingesting after revoke.

unknown: Whether token issue/revoke or reads are audit-logged

authentication.summary: An OAuth application's client ID/secret is exchanged at POST /v1/oauth/token for a 15-minute opaque bearer token scoped to users.view, users.suspend and/or users.reactivate.

federation.details: Client credentials grant only; no workload identity federation documented.

ip_restriction.boundary: No IP restriction for OAuth apps documented.

lifetime.summary: Access token 15 min; client secret no stated expiry

renewal.expiry_basis: No refresh tokens; request a new access token with client credentials
renewal.summary: Secret rotation keeps the old secret valid 6 hours.

administration.summary: Owners, admins or Security group members create OAuth apps under Integrations > OAuth Application. Scopes fixed at creation.
administration.conditions: Business or Enterprise Password Manager, not Teams; not supported with automated provisioning.

offboard.details: Client credentials belong to an OAuth application integration, not a user.

inventory.details: 1Password.com Integrations page shows active OAuth Applications.

usage.ui: 1Password.com > Audit Log > Try new audit log; look for actor 'Oauth app' (user.suspend, user.reactivate)
usage.api: GET /api/v3/auditevents (Events API beta; filter results on actor and action user.suspend / user.reactivate)

token_format.notes: From documented example access token; opaque.

credential_id_fields.notes: Introspect only for own app's tokens

containment.steps: Integrations > OAuth Application > Revoke integration (kills all tokens), or POST /v1/oauth/revoke per token.
containment.notes: Revoke integration revokes all access tokens.

unknown: Audit events for OAuth app create/rotate/revoke
Whether Users API reads are logged
